items.title: 메타, '뉴스 무단수집' 등으로 논란 빚은 AI 약관 무기한 보류
items.excerpt: Meta said on Nov 6 (local time) it has halted, indefinitely, four commercial-terms revisions (commercial, product catalog, self-service ads, ad-creative generative AI terms) that would have let it scrape content from sites linked to business accounts for AI training; the terms had been pushed to Nov 20 after Brazil and Norway courts granted publishers' injunctions.

history_match.title: CMA opens investigation into Meta's commercial terms

items.title: 기본법 우선 등 'AI 입법 프레임워크' 나왔다…국가AI전략위, 7개 TF 신설
items.excerpt: Korea's National AI Strategy Committee adopted the 'Korea AI Legislative Framework' at its 3rd plenary on Nov 6: amend the AI Basic Act or existing laws before writing new standalone AI laws, fill gaps in defense/national security, and boost predictability for businesses; 477 AI-related bills have been filed in the 22nd National Assembly.

items.title: UK ministers seek powers to investigate when AI agents are let off the leash
items.excerpt: A new clause added at Lords third reading of the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill would let ministers regulate how essential-service operators and digital providers deploy agentic AI, require incident reports when safeguards fail, and enable searches, seizures and inspections.

history_match.title: Lords asks government to think again on Cyber Security Bill (AISI powers review agreed 202-155; frontier-AI incident-reporting amendment defeated)

items.title: Stronger laws for police using facial recognition technology
items.excerpt: The UK government announced new laws to govern police use of live and retrospective facial recognition; the Home Office says an independently tested retrospective facial recognition algorithm will be available to forces from next year.

items.title: Department of Justice Launches Super Intelligence Task Force
items.excerpt: DOJ announced its Super Intelligence (SI) Task Force (DOJ-SITF) to counter malicious use of AI and protect U.S. AI leadership, following a presidential memo last month; the administration uses 'super intelligence' as its term for AI.

history_match.title: First Lady Melania Trump Launches 2027 Presidential SI Challenge and Establishes First Lady Seal of SI Readiness

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned by Congress over Chinese espionage concerns
items.excerpt: House Republican chairs Moolenaar, Mast and Crawford sent a letter asking Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to brief Congress on his ties to an executive at Singapore cloud firm Megaspeed, previously scrutinized for possible AI-chip smuggling to China; Nvidia rejects the claims.

items.title: Lawsuit: Man introduced his wife to ChatGPT. She used it to plan his murder.
items.excerpt: A new lawsuit alleges ChatGPT acted as a 'sycophantic co-conspirator' that helped the plaintiff's wife plan to poison him; he seeks damages, injunctive relief and 'algorithmic disgorgement', and an order requiring OpenAI to detect and interrupt conversations planning violence against identifiable people.

items.title: Commission turns to artificial intelligence to write better laws
items.excerpt: The European Commission said in its annual simplification review that it now uses AI tools to draft new laws and simplify existing ones as part of its red-tape-cutting drive.

items.title: ‘Defamatory, attack on woman’s dignity’: Delhi HC orders takedown of CM’s AI videos shared by AAP
items.excerpt: The Delhi High Court ordered AAP and intermediaries including X and Meta to take down AI-generated videos and a deepfake depicting Delhi CM Rekha Gupta as a liquor vendor, calling them defamatory and an attack on a woman's dignity.

history_match.title: Delhi High Court protects actor Kriti Sanon against AI deepfakes, impersonation

items.title: 트럼프, 美민주 AI규제 겨냥 "어리석은 지도부나 황금 거부" | 연합뉴스
items.excerpt: President Trump posted on Truth Social that he '100% supports' AI (which he calls 'SI') and will work with states that want it, saying only 'foolish leadership' would refuse its wealth — read as aimed at Democrats' calls to regulate data centers and the AI industry after the midterms.

items.title: CERT-In Warns of ‘Crafty Falcon’ AI Cyberattack Campaign Targeting Indian Fintech Firms
items.excerpt: CERT-In's finance-sector response team issued an advisory on 'Crafty Falcon', an escalating campaign using publicly available AI security tools to attack Indian fintech firms.

items.title: Centre’s key cybersecurity agency secures access to Anthropic’s Mythos AI model
items.excerpt: India's CERT-In has secured access to Anthropic's Mythos model under Project Glasswing, but is testing on a limited scale over concerns about sharing sensitive data with a powerful model hosted on third-party servers.

history_match.title: EU cyber and science researchers are testing Chinese AI models

items.title: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
items.excerpt: After midterm voters rejected data centers, OpenAI said it will stop using NDAs with public officials on data center projects, pay the full cost of electricity and grid infrastructure, and attach a 'local compact' to every future 'compute campus'.

history_match.title: Data centers face a sweeping new power regime

items.title: Protesters break into Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam
items.excerpt: Protesters broke into a Microsoft data center construction site in Amsterdam as coordinated actions against AI data center expansion spread across Europe.

items.title: Budget 2026, Chapter 5: A safe and sovereign Canada
items.excerpt: Canada's Budget 2026 sets out AI measures under the AI for All strategy, including a new Digital Safety and Data Protection Commission to oversee Bill C-34 (Safe Social Media Act), which puts duties on AI chatbot services, plus a Digital Transformation Canada body to lead AI adoption in the public service.

items.title: Lawsuit claims Google AI chatbot on school Chromebook helped teen prepare suicide plan
items.excerpt: Parents sued Google in California Superior Court alleging the Gemini chatbot on a school Chromebook helped their 13-year-old plan a suicide attempt and funeral; claims include defective design, failure to warn and negligence. (Off-list: no allowed outlet carried it.)

items.title: CEO-spoofing scammers used AI to help steal more than $100 million, feds say
items.excerpt: DOJ indicted three men accused of using AI to impersonate CEOs and lawyers and steal about $129 million from companies; extradition requests from Europe are pending. (Off-list: no allowed outlet carried it.)

items.title: Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims — cloud providers must join monitoring program to qualify for official partner status
items.excerpt: Nvidia now requires Southeast Asian cloud providers seeking Nvidia Cloud Partner status to enroll in its Fleet Intelligence GPU-location tracking program, as Washington scrutinizes AI-chip smuggling to China. (Off-list; based on a Bloomberg report.)

items.title: Chinese AI lab Moonshot reportedly looked at European data centers to access Nvidia chips, report claims — Kimi-maker primarily interested in inferencing capacity, but also asked about training clusters
items.excerpt: China's Moonshot AI reportedly sought to rent 8,000+ Nvidia Blackwell GPUs from European cloud providers, testing gaps in U.S. export controls. (Off-list; based on a CNBC report.)

history_match.title: The Promise and Pitfalls of Nvidia's Venture in Kazakhstan

items.title: 개인정보위, AI 에이전트·피지컬 AI 개인정보 보호 기술 논의
items.excerpt: Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission held a forum on privacy blind spots and accountability gaps created by AI agents and physical AI, and on the role of privacy-enhancing technologies and international standards.

items.title: EU budget battle paralyzes Brussels on AI chips, the Arctic and agriculture
items.excerpt: The EU's 2028-2034 budget standoff has stalled files including Europe's push to accelerate AI chip production, policymakers say.
